$comment: Generated by scripts/gen-marketing-visuals.mjs from components.manifest.json, platform-parity.json, block-parity.json and the real token output. Do not hand-edit: regenerate with `pnpm gen:visuals`. Every count here is derived, so no asset can carry a number the product has moved past.

assets.note: Constructed illustration, not a screenshot of a real app. Values are illustrative and labelled as such.
assets.alt: Two rows of three panels — Web, iOS and Android. On day one all three show padding 16, radius 12 and the same accent colour. At month six each has drifted in a different property: web padding 20, iOS radius 16, Android a different accent. Caption: each change was locally correct, none was written anywhere the others could see.

A single DTCG token source feeding a generator, which produces four outputs: CSS custom properties for web, Swift constants for iOS, Kotlin objects for Android and Dart constants for Flutter. Caption notes the generated files are committed build artifacts, so one value change moves every platform in one commit.

A component contract at the top with dashed arrows down to 5 independent implementations — React 98 of 98, Angular 64 of 98, SwiftUI 90 of 98, Jetpack Compose 90 of 98, Flutter 90 of 98 — each labelled hand-written. Caption: dashed arrows mean implements, not compiles into.

A pipeline reading claim, source, check, CI, public. Below it three real examples: a component claiming SwiftUI checked by check:platform-source; a docs page showing Compose code checked by check:platform-code; a registry item's files checked by check:registry-deps. Each fails the build when the claim outruns the source.

A coverage table with one row per platform: React, 98 of 98, package stable, installable from npm; Angular, 64 of 98, package preview, installable from npm; SwiftUI, 90 of 98, package stable, not installable — build from source; Jetpack Compose, 90 of 98, package stable, not installable — build from source; Flutter, 90 of 98, package stable, not installable — build from source. Footer: 97 components plus 1 documented recipe, 20 blocks, generated from the manifest.

Three adoption rungs. One, tokens: keep every component you have, highlighted and marked you can stop here. Two, components: copy what you need, the CLI writes source into your repo. Three, blocks: whole composed patterns with real source per platform.

Two columns presented as equals. Left, one runtime: your code into a drawing layer into every platform, cost at the edges. Right, native implementations: a shared contract into five implementations in each platform's idiom, cost in the maintenance.

components.manifest.json at the centre with arrows out to four surfaces: coverage table, component pages, platform docs and marketing copy. A dashed arrow from check:platform-source points back at the manifest. Caption: it found a component claiming three native platforms with an implementation on none.

assets.note: GitHub social preview. Upload is a repository setting — manual action.
assets.alt: KinetixUI social preview. Heading: a design system for teams on more than one platform, with cross-platform claims verified against source in CI. React 98 of 98, on npm; Angular 64 of 98, on npm; SwiftUI 90 of 98, from source; Jetpack Compose 90 of 98, from source; Flutter 90 of 98, from source. MIT.
